title: Durable task continuity, decision history and verification evidence
context: ScopeHub is a long-lived product maintained with substantial AI participation. Conversation memory, milestone labels and an overwritten local test report do not provide sufficient continuity or evidence for future changes.
decision: Use a Git-versioned JSON task ledger and check catalog, validated ADR relationships, per-run harness reports and selectively archived task evidence. Keep one source of truth for each responsibility and make the next executable action visible to a new agent.
authority: The owner explicitly requests task, ADR, harness and scaffold foundations for sustained product development. This changes repository workflow without changing product runtime, permissions or wire protocols.

alternatives.option: Rely on conversation history and the last local report
alternatives.reason: It loses task dependencies, rationale and the identity of previously verified code across sessions and machines.

alternatives.option: Introduce an external task service or a custom workflow platform immediately
alternatives.reason: Current work can be represented and checked locally; accounts, synchronization and another runtime are not yet justified.

consequences: Agents maintain meaningful work items with outcomes, scope, dependencies, acceptance, verification and a next action. Small edits can remain inside an existing task.
Task completion is historical: it names the task definition and tested execution inputs. Current readiness requires current checks as well.
Reports retain run IDs, environment, commands, log digests and source identities. Compact task receipts are tracked; full local logs remain under .reports and CI uploads them.
A dirty-worktree digest identifies tested bytes but does not independently preserve them. Release artifacts require a committed source revision and retained build/acceptance evidence.
The check catalog drives the harness and acceptance mapping. A planned or unsupported-platform check remains blocked, never passed.

Accepted ADR rationale is preserved. A changed decision gets a new record with supersedes links; current interpretation is derived rather than rewriting an old choice as though it had always been current.
Repository controls verify record consistency and observed execution, not semantic correctness by themselves. Tests and review must substantiate the stated acceptance criteria.
decision_triggers: Changes to language ownership, process boundaries, permissions or protocols follow the existing owner-approval rule.
Record durable choices with material migration, replacement, data-ownership or operating consequences, including reversals.
Routine implementation inside accepted boundaries uses task records and checks without an additional approval ceremony.

history_policy.tasks: Keep completed and cancelled IDs and their evidence/reasons. Introduce a new task for a changed outcome instead of rewriting the definition of completed work.
history_policy.decisions: Use proposed, accepted or rejected records. An accepted successor may supersede an accepted predecessor; preserve both records and their rationale.
history_policy.source: Git commits preserve implementation history; task evidence binds a completion claim to the tested content and available Git revision.
history_policy.verification: Execution snapshots exclude task state, evidence receipts and decision/review metadata to avoid self-reference; the project validator checks that metadata independently on every check and status call.
history_policy.release: Retain installer/build identity, dependency versions, notices and actual acceptance results with a release. Local or mock checks do not grant real-data, model, installation or release acceptance.

lifecycle_requirements: Version protocol and persisted formats; add migration and recovery checks when persistent state is introduced.
Capture model, prompt, tool and dataset versions when they influence a result, and maintain replayable collaboration evaluations.
Treat product incidents and escaped defects as tasks with regression evidence when the failure warrants a check.
Validate backup/restore and upgrade behavior before shipping a persisted-data change; define a recovery route for unsupported downgrades.
Review dependencies and licenses at integration and release boundaries; select additional automation when it serves an actual maintenance need.
revisit_when: Concurrent work requires coordination that Git and explicit task dependencies cannot represent adequately.
Task lookup or selective evidence retention becomes costly enough to justify indexed tooling.
Actual release and incident workflows reveal missing traceability or verification.
